title: Matroid secretary conjecture
formal: Does there exist a universal constant \(C\ge 1\) such that every finite matroid M admits a randomized online selection strategy which, for every assignment of nonnegative weights to its elements, returns an independent set of expected weight at least \(\operatorname{OPT}(M,w)/C\) when the elements arrive in a uniformly random order?
definitions: A matroid is a finite set E and a nonempty family \(I\subseteq 2^{E}\) closed under subsets and satisfying augmentation: if \(A,B\in I\) and |\(A|<|B|\), some \(b\in B\setminus A\) has \(A\cup \{b\}\in I\). The strategy knows E and I in advance, but not the weights. A fixed adversary assigns \(w:E\to \mathbb{R} _{\ge 0}\) before the order and strategy coins are sampled. Upon each arrival its identity and weight are revealed. The strategy must accept or reject it irrevocably before the next arrival, keeping the accepted set in I. \(\operatorname{OPT}(M,w)=\max _{S\in I}\sum _{e\in S}w(e)\). Expectation includes a uniformly random permutation of E and the strategy’s independent random coins. There is no computation or oracle-query bound; this is the competitive-existence conjecture for the full-information matroid model.

context_blocks.text: The general matroid secretary problem asks whether random arrival order is enough to recover a constant fraction of a best feasible weighted set without seeing future weights. It unifies classical secretary selection with broad independence constraints.
The random-assignment model also randomizes where weights are placed, and admits stronger results. Those results do not settle the adversarial-assignment, random-arrival model used here.

why: The main unresolved competitive-ratio question for online selection under general matroid constraints.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
